invariants.name: A guard error denies a merge or work-loss call
Write checks keep running on repo files and skip scratch files

abstraction.hides: The per-call canonical folder cache for profile and git root reads, the node bindings of file, git and profile operations, and the child_process invocation details of runProcess.
callersKnow: processPorts returns one Ports value that caches readProfile and gitRoot per canonical folder for one hook call.
Context.ports is required and HookDeps takes ports: () => Ports so runHook and runCursorHook build one edge value per call.
runProcess returns Result<ProcessOutput, StartFailure> and never throws on a missing binary or failed start.
abstraction.deletionTest: Without ports.ts and process.ts, each hook handler and helper reads files, git and the profile directly and invokes spawnSync on its own, repeating profile reads up to 7 times per hook call and blocking replay tests.

alternatives.name: Keep direct disk reads and test through temp repos
alternatives.rejectedBecause: Handlers can bypass test fakes by reading the disk directly, and no replay test can run with the repo deleted.

alternatives.name: Module-level profile cache
alternatives.rejectedBecause: Module state leaks across hook calls and test runs.

alternatives.name: Optional Context.ports with a disk fallback
alternatives.rejectedBecause: A handler or test can silently omit the port and read the disk directly.

omitted: SessionGuards does not model the port cache or replay harness. The laws in B35.md and their controls in ports.test.ts, process.test.ts and hook-port-replay.test.ts guard those properties.
State folder stores, GitHub API factories and principle skill lookups stay outside Ports.

bounds: Attended and unattended sessions, four base authorities, three working-tree authorities, two PRs, two channels, a guard error or none, and prompts of one or two of seven clause classes from four sources.
Each combination of four path facts for one write and an optional commit.
Each set of changes from four change kinds in three places, and 16 git commands with their documented effects.
One repo at the path that the session makes, one record of that path, its settle window, and a repo of another process that appears after the window.
A HEAD whose gates pass or fail under the base profile or an edited profile, one gate run, and one push or commit with or without a hook skip to three targets.

negative.defect: The destructive guard passes a hook-skip push whose gate record holds another profile blob than the source and its merge base, so a push under an edited profile skips the git hooks.

limits: A helper outside src/astack/hook/ can still read the disk on a branch that no replay fixture exercises.
State folder stores stay direct, so handlers that touch state keep fs-write.
Exact-head CI, review, Shipping and every ordinary gate stay required.
